key_concepts: Earthquakes release stored crustal energy and generate seismic waves from the epicenter.
Earthquake magnitude influences the amount of community damage.
Underwater earthquakes at subduction zones can displace water and form tsunamis.
Tsunamis are series of ocean waves that can surge over 100 feet onto land.
Body waves include P-waves and S-waves and travel through Earth's interior.
P-waves are compressional and travel through solids, liquids, and gases.
S-waves are shear waves that only travel through solid materials.
Surface waves travel along Earth's surface and cause most earthquake damage.
Rayleigh waves move particles in an elliptical vertical motion.
Love waves move particles horizontally perpendicular to wave direction.
Run-up is the vertical water height a tsunami pushes above normal sea level.
Inundation is the horizontal inland distance and flooding caused by a tsunami.
